title: Ethnobotanical survey of anti-asthmatic plants in South Western Nigeria
licence: open access; article-specific reuse terms not stated in the PDF
notes: The article reports herbarium identification, but Table 1 does not publish per-row voucher identifiers. Therapeutic claims are retained only as source context and are not exported to the runtime lookup.

title: Ethnobotanical Studies of Port Harcourt Metropolis, Nigeria
notes: All 84 displayed rows are included after adjudicating the two defects that held the table in staged review. Serials run 1-83 with no gap and no duplicate, and one further row carries no serial at all: the article's "83 species" counts the numbered rows, while Table 1 displays 84. The unnumbered row is Acanthus montanus, complete and taxonomically resolvable, so it is kept with serial_as_published null and its unnumbered_source_row flag rather than discarded. Three rows print the botanical name in the common-name column and the common name in the botanical column (serials 47, 48, 49 - Azadirachta indica, Moringa oleifera, Persea americana); GBIF matches the common-name cell to an accepted species and the botanical cell to nothing in all three, so the values are recorded under the attribute they describe and what each column printed is kept verbatim in source_columns_as_printed. Two species are listed twice by the authors (Capsicum annuum, Cymbopogon citratus) with differing vernacular spellings; both printings are kept. Seven rows carry a botanical name that does not resolve to an accepted species - misspellings such as Telfaria occidentalis and Dioscoreae cayennensis, and one genus-only 'Grewia sp' - and are left uncorrected, so the build withholds them as taxonomy_unresolved rather than this file guessing at what the authors meant. As with the other surveys, the per-row therapeutic indications are retained as published source text and are not exported.

title: Ethnobotanical Survey of Plants Used for Treating Cough Associated with Respiratory Conditions in Ede South Local Government Area of Osun State, Nigeria
notes: Table 2 heads its local-name column "Local Name (Yoruba)" and is unnumbered, so the row locator is the ordinal position. Parts and preparations are joined from Appendix Table A1 by species. Two entries printed in the Yoruba column are not Yoruba names (bamboo; Ugu, which is Igbo) and are kept as published text without becoming mappings. The runtime index uses the name mappings, parts and preparations, not the cough indication or the fidelity indices.

title: Ethnobotanical Survey of Medicinal Plants Used in the Treatment of COVID-19 and Related Respiratory Infections in Ogbomosho South and North Local Government Areas, Oyo State, Nigeria
notes: All 86 rows of Tables 2, 3 and 4 (COVID-19, cough, flu) are preserved, each with its own table locator, but production export is blocked pending botanical review. The local-name column is unlabelled; the methods state that names were collected in Yoruba. Several determinations disagree with the other registered sources for the same Yoruba name: Egbeesi as Neonauclea excelsa (Egbesi is Nauclea latifolia in two surveys), Iyere as Piper nigrum (Piper guineense in two sources), Asofeyeje as Nigella sativa (Rauvolfia vomitoria in two sources), Epo aganwo as Drypetes gossweileri (Oganwo is a Khaya in three sources). The build only detects a disagreement between identical spellings, so including the table as it stands would export some of these as resolved mappings. The COVID-19, cough and flu indications are survey context only.

title: Indigenous medicinal plants used in folk medicine for malaria treatment in Kwara State, Nigeria: an ethnobotanical study
notes: All 62 rows are preserved, but production export is blocked pending language review. Only six rows label their names Yoruba or Nupe; the other 56 state no language, interviews were conducted in both, and at least one unlabelled name is Hausa (Karandafi) and one is a nickname (June 12). Unlabelled names are staged with a null language.

title: Ethnobotanical uses of plants in Nigeria: an analysis of current research trends and patterns
notes: Table 2 is retained as a catalogue of 79 original studies to acquire. Table 3 is retained as secondary review evidence only and cannot produce runtime mappings.

title: Medicinal Plants in Tropical West Africa

notes: Retained for botanical, synonym, pharmacology, and bibliographic checking. The book does not provide a structured language-labelled vernacular index, so no local-name mappings were inferred from its prose.

title: Handbook of African Medicinal Plants, Second Edition
notes: Only concise mapping facts and page locators are staged. Runtime export is blocked because most vernacular labels lack a row-specific country or locality and have not been reviewed by language practitioners.

title: Sanko practitioner-confirmed vernacular mappings
notes: Local names Sanko could not place botanically, reviewed and confirmed by a named practitioner or the research team through scripts/plant-review.js. Each entry carries a pseudonymous reviewer reference and the number of times the name was seen in use; the source transcripts stay out of this file and out of the repository. This is the only plant source whose evidence is a practitioner's own statement rather than a publication, which is why it is ingested under its own status rather than as 'included' alongside the surveys.

title: Europe PMC and Crossref primary-source discovery
licence: index metadata only; each candidate carries its own licence
notes: Written by scripts/discover-sources.js. A ranked list of Nigerian ethnobotanical sources to acquire, and the resolution of the 79 original studies catalogued in anumudu-2025-nigeria-review to DOIs, licences and full texts. Candidates are citations, not data: no row here produces a vernacular mapping, and an acquired source only becomes ingestable when it is registered in this file in its own right.

title: Wikidata taxon labels in Nigerian languages
notes: Written by scripts/import-wikidata-vernaculars.js. Labels are crowd-sourced and unsourced — no locality, no collector, no citation — and a large share of those returned in an African language are the botanical or English name filed in the wrong language. They are candidates for review, never mappings. A candidate reaches the runtime index only through practitioner confirmation, attributed to the reviewer who confirmed it and carrying the candidate source it came from.

title: Ethnobotanical survey and conservation of the indigenous plants used for traditional orthopedic care practices in Bayelsa Central Senatorial District, Nigeria
licence: diamond open access; no reuse licence stated in the article, on the journal site, or in Crossref and OpenAlex metadata
notes: The first Ijaw source in the index, and the second South-South one. Table 2 prints the English common name and the Ijaw name in a single cell separated by a slash, in either order and sometimes only one of the two, so scripts/extract-bayelsa-survey.js lists the thirty-six English names read off the table and treats everything else in the cell as Ijaw; the cell is kept verbatim in vernacular_as_published. Two cells yield no Ijaw name: 'Hospital too far' is the Nigerian English by-name for Jatropha tanjorensis, and 'Native pop' an English name for Ficus lutea. Table 3 gives preparation and treatment in prose rather than a parts column, so no plant parts are claimed, and its therapeutic text is not exported. Ingested on the same terms as sonibare-2008-anti-asthmatic: freely readable with no reuse licence stated anywhere, and only the published name mappings are used.

title: Ethno medicinal survey of plants used by the indigenes of Rivers State of Nigeria

localities: all local government areas of Rivers State

licence: free to read at the publisher (bronze open access); no reuse licence stated by the publisher or recorded in Crossref, OpenAlex or Europe PMC
extraction_method: transcribed from page scans in two passes (the species table, then the plant-part column); the PDF has no text layer and no OCR was used
notes: 188 species from 460 households across every local government area of Rivers State, and the largest South-South source in the index. Local names are printed with the language in brackets, in the four languages the paper names: Ikwerre (83 names), Kalabari (38), Ekpeye (31) and Ogoni (32). Ikwerre, Kalabari and Ekpeye map onto ISO 639-3 as ikw, ijn and ekp. Ogoni does not: it names a cluster - Khana, Gokana, Eleme, Baan, Tee - so those rows keep the published label in language_as_published and carry no language code, rather than this file choosing one the paper does not state. Four rows print no language at all, and one repeats the botanical name in the local-name column ('Aloe vera') and so yields no mapping. Two pairs of specimens share a merged cell (PNM 24/25 and 44/45) and are paired in the printed order; all four are flagged. The article is a scan with no text layer, so Table 1 was transcribed from the page images and the transcription is committed at surveys/transcriptions/ as the form this repository rebuilds from. Botanical names are checked by GBIF downstream, where a misreading surfaces as an unresolved name; a misreading in a local name cannot be checked by anything, which is the cost of using a scan. The plant-part column was transcribed in a second pass and parsed against a vocabulary of part terms; all 188 cells parse with no leftover text. Ingested on the same terms as sonibare-2008-anti-asthmatic and olatokunbo-2022-bayelsa: freely readable, reuse terms unstated, only the published name mappings used.
